_scope_note: REVISED 2026-09-12 after the velo-pr-gate run on PR #2104 found that plan-side renaming alone leaves plan and record disagreeing. Absorbs #2108 (execution-side namers) so the two land atomically: shipping EXPR$<n> in the plan while execution still emits Multiply_price_quantity replaces an obvious placeholder (__expr__) with a plausible-looking wrong name, which is worse than the defect. One defect, one landing. PR #2104 is superseded by the PR this spec produces; its two commits (plan side + SelectField::Column) are reviewed and may be used as a reference implementation of bars 1-6.
_why: Unaliased computed SELECT items were all named __expr__ and unaliased GROUP BY keys __group__, so two computed items in one query produced duplicate, unreferenceable output names. A first attempt fixed the PLAN only (PR #2104, closed); the gate showed that leaves the plan and the emitted record disagreeing — schema EXPR$0 vs record Multiply_price_quantity — which is worse than the defect, because __expr__ was visibly a placeholder while EXPR$0 looks like a real referenceable name nothing downstream can use. Three generators name the same expression three ways and are coupled through PlanNode::Aggregate::alias_keys, which is also the runtime aggregate lookup key: changing the plan side alone failed 48 tests. So plan and execution naming are one task, and this spec absorbs #2108.
acceptance: No occurrence of the string __expr__ or __group__ remains in src/

An unaliased SELECT item whose expression is not a column reference is named EXPR$<n>, n = zero-based position in the select list, and that is the name in BOTH the propagated plan schema AND the emitted record. This INCLUDES function calls and aggregates: SELECT SUM(value) yields EXPR$0, not SUM(value). That is Flink and ksqlDB behaviour (EXPR$0 / KSQL_COL_0) and the positional uniqueness is the property the issue's prior-art section identifies as the whole point. A mixed rule — conventional names for functions, positional for everything else — was considered and REJECTED: it re-admits the defect through SUM(price * qty), which renders SUM(expr) today, so two such items collide exactly as two __expr__ items did. A test asserts equality of the two through a real engine consumer, not by comparing two plan-side helpers.

A GROUP BY key that is not a column reference AND appears in the SELECT list carries its SELECT-list position (EXPR$<n>), because the output column IS the SELECT item. A computed GROUP BY key that is NOT in the SELECT list is named GROUP$<n> by its GROUP BY index — a SEPARATE namespace, deliberately. Two independent positional counters in one namespace collide: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY price * quantity would name the group slot EXPR$0 (group index 0) and COUNT(*) EXPR$0 (select index 0), and output_schema appends group fields before aggregates, so the schema would carry two EXPR$0 fields — the exact duplicate-name defect this issue exists to remove, with collision handling forbidden. GROUP$<n> cannot collide with EXPR$<n> by construction, needs no dedup, and is honest: that slot exists so HAVING can resolve against it, not as a user-visible output column.

builder.rs::select_fields_to_project_exprs and schema_propagation.rs::schema_from_select_fields call ONE shared naming helper for EVERY SelectField variant — Expression, Column, AliasedColumn, Wildcard. Neither holds a private copy of any arm. SelectField::Column must strip its qualifier at both sites via the shared helper: the parser never emits this variant, so no parsed query exercises it, which is exactly how it drifted.

An unaliased SelectField::Expression holding a plain column reference resolves to its bare column name at BOTH sites (before this change schema_propagation.rs returns __expr__ for this case and builder.rs does not)
No collision handling is added: no suffix bump, no rename, no duplicate detection — a comment at the generator records that #1919 owns that check

EXPR$<n> is the name at execution too. AccumulatorManager::generate_field_name and SelectProcessor::get_expression_name no longer produce a competing output name for an unaliased computed expression: either they delegate to the shared helper, or they are demoted to a documented runtime LOOKUP key that is never an output name and never reaches a Schema. Whichever is chosen, exactly one code path decides what an output column is called.

expr_to_string's `_ => "expr"` catch-all no longer reaches any output name. Two computed SELECT items must never both be named "expr" at any layer. If the catch-all survives as a lookup-key detail, a comment states why it cannot escape to a schema.

The alias_keys write/read contract is preserved or migrated atomically. PlanNode::Aggregate::alias_keys is the key the runtime aggregate evaluator looks up, so renaming the plan side while execution still looks up the old key is silent wrong-output, not a test failure, in any path the pass_to_stay tests do not cover. Record in agent.log as an ALIAS-KEYS line which of the two (preserve / migrate) was done and how it was verified, and repeat it in the final report. The caller copies it into the PR body — the worker does not open the PR.

Every coupled test passes at the end. There is deliberately NO enumerated list to check against — an earlier bar said 'all 48 tests listed in #2108 pass without modification', but that list lives only in a closed issue and the number is stale (54 after the plan side was fully migrated), so it could not tell a worker which edits were prohibited. The RULE decides instead: a legacy generated name on an UNALIASED item may be updated, one CHANGED-EXPECTATION line each stating why the old name was wrong; an explicit AS alias or a non-naming property may NOT be touched and its failure is stop condition 3. Green sweep plus one rationale line per changed expectation is the completion evidence.

walk_expr_for_aggs's internal aggregate lookup key is not changed incidentally. Its own comment states it must match the runtime evaluator's lookup key; if the unification changes it, that is a deliberate, stated decision.
New tests are registered in the parent mod.rs

docs/sql/PARSER_GRAMMAR.md documents the generated-name rule alongside the select_item production (issue #1918 acceptance bar 4) — this is a REQUIRED doc change, distinct from the forbidden corpus-editing below. It must describe the SHIPPED behaviour, including that the name holds at execution.
./run-commit.sh --fast is green, and any cargo fmt rewrite it applies is committed

Each of the 8 fail_to_pass tests (explicit_alias_survives_positional_naming is NOT among them — it is the exempt guard) was written BEFORE the fix, run red, and its failure recorded in agent.log as a RED-FIRST line carrying the actual assertion message. None of the six exists on master, so a test written after the fix proves only that the code does what it does. The earlier attempt at this issue shipped a group-by test that passed both before and after the change because it constructed Aggregate with empty select_exprs/alias_keys and never reached the path it claimed to cover.

If any of the 8 fail_to_pass tests passes against unfixed code, STOP and report rather than loosening the test until it fails. Either the test does not reach the path it claims to cover, or the bar's premise is wrong — a human decides which.

An explicit AS alias always wins and is never replaced by a generated name: SELECT SUM(value) AS total emits total. This is the user's escape hatch from positional names and the reason renaming unaliased items is safe; a test pinning an AS alias must therefore keep passing unchanged.

Two unaliased computed aggregates get DISTINCT names: SELECT SUM(a * b), SUM(c * d) emits EXPR$0 and EXPR$1, never SUM(expr) twice. This shape is the aggregate form of the issue's defect and is pinned by its own test.

A test that pins a LEGACY GENERATED name for an UNALIASED item — SUM(...), SUM(expr), __expr__, __group__, price_Multiply_quantity — may have its expectation updated, with a CHANGED-EXPECTATION line per test stating that the old name was wrong because it was either non-positional or colliding. A test that pins an EXPLICIT AS alias, or any non-naming property (row counts, values, ordering, watermarks), must NOT be updated; if such a test fails, that is a real regression and a STOP.

cargo fmt --all is run and its result committed BEFORE any STOP, not only at the gate. Both prior runs stopped before reaching run-commit.sh, so neither ever formatted, and CI failed at cargo fmt --all -- --check before reaching a single test. A dispatch that stops early ships unformatted code unless fmt is unconditional.

A test named explicit_alias_survives_positional_naming exists and passes, asserting SELECT SUM(value) AS total still emits total. It is a GUARD, not a regression test, and is deliberately NOT in fail_to_pass: explicit aliases already work on master, so the test passes before and after and can never be run red. Exempt from the red-first requirement for that reason — do not try to make it fail, and do not report it under stop condition 4.

EVIDENCE STANDARD, stated because two prohibitions cannot be diff-verified: that a rewritten assertion still tests what it did before, and that no non-naming behaviour moved, are established by (a) a green unit sweep, (b) one CHANGED-EXPECTATION line per edited test saying why the OLD expectation was wrong, and (c) the three alias canaries passing unchanged. That is evidence, not proof, and the spec does not pretend otherwise. velo-pr-gate should spot-check a sample of the CHANGED-EXPECTATION rationales against the actual diff rather than accepting the count.

CHANGED-EXPECTATION lines must RECONCILE against the diff, which makes the otherwise-unverifiable prohibition checkable: the number of pre-existing test functions whose assertion lines the diff modifies must EQUAL the number of CHANGED-EXPECTATION lines in agent.log. Report both counts in the final report. A modified assertion with no matching line is a silently weakened test; a line with no matching diff hunk is a rationale for a change that was not made. Either mismatch is a STOP. This replaces 'trust the rationales' with an arithmetic check a reviewer can rerun.

HUNK AUDIT — the shape of every expectation edit is constrained, which makes 'does the assertion still test the same thing' diff-checkable rather than a matter of trust. Inside a PRE-EXISTING test, exactly TWO edit shapes are permitted: (1) a legacy generated-name string literal ("SUM(value)", "SUM(expr)", "__expr__", "__group__", "__agg__", "price_Multiply_quantity") becomes the corresponding EXPR$<n> or GROUP$<n> literal; (2) a QUALIFIED column output name loses its qualifier ("orders.order_id" -> "order_id"), which bars 4 and 5 require now that SelectField::Column routes through the shared helper — an earlier version of this bar permitted only shape (1) and would have false-flagged three correct edits in join_groupby_index tests. On such a line nothing else may change — no numbers, no comparison operators, no expected counts — and no assertion may be added or removed from the test body. Reformatting a multi-line assert onto one line because the literal got shorter is shape-preserving and fine. Anything else is either a real regression being papered over or a different change smuggled in, and is a STOP.

No output schema contains two fields with the same generated name. A test covers SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY price * quantity specifically, asserting the group slot and the aggregate do not collide.

RESIDUAL RISK, stated rather than prohibited: that no UNCOVERED row-count, ordering, watermark or value behaviour moved cannot be established by any check available here, so the spec does not claim it. What IS established: the hunk audit constrains every expectation edit to a name-literal substitution, the unit sweep is green, and the three alias canaries pass unchanged. A prohibition the spec cannot verify would be theatre; naming the gap lets velo-pr-gate decide whether to sample further.

__agg__ (UNNAMED_AGGREGATE_PLACEHOLDER) no longer appears as an output name in any plan schema: an unaliased top-level aggregate slot carries the same EXPR$<n> the runtime emits. It was initially scoped out, which contradicted bar 2 — a plan that says __agg__ while the record says EXPR$0 is exactly the plan/record divergence this issue exists to close.

SHELL HAZARD — EXPR$<n> and GROUP$<n> contain '$', so an unquoted shell context expands them: GROUP$0 becomes GROUPbash because $0 is the shell name. That already corrupted one recorded expectation during this issue's own work (failed-with=... right: "GROUPbash"). Always SINGLE-quote these names in shell commands, -E filters and log lines. A test asserting GROUPbash or EXPRbash is a corrupted expectation, not a finding.
forbidden: No NEW collision handling: do not make the shared naming helper consult any collection of already-used names. This does NOT forbid code that already does so — group_by_columnar.rs::expr_fname_collision already scans the SELECT list via legacy_expr_fname/get_expression_name, and that pre-existing fallback stays. The rule is that EXPR$<n> itself derives from position alone and gains no dedup logic — no HashSet/HashMap/Vec::contains of prior names, no numeric suffix appended to a generated name, no retry loop on a name. EXPR$<n> derives from position ALONE. #1919 owns duplicate detection.
Do not implement NB-005 duplicate-output-name detection — no new error variant, no new check in sql/validation/name_binding.rs. That is #1919.
Do not touch __exists__, __raw__, __velostream_variant, or __agg__ — zero diff lines containing those four strings.

Do not change a line inside a ```sql fence under docs/ or demo/. Prose changes to docs/sql/PARSER_GRAMMAR.md outside such a fence are REQUIRED work; editing an example so a validator stops complaining is the escape hatch this closes.
Do not add #[cfg(test)] or #[test] inside src/ — zero such lines added under src/.

Do not weaken an existing test. The diff-checkable part: no #[test] removed, no #[ignore] added, no assert*! line deleted from a pre-existing test. The part that is NOT diff-checkable: whether a rewritten assertion still tests what it did before — that is judged per test by its CHANGED-EXPECTATION line, which is why each one must state why the OLD expectation was wrong. The 48 coupled tests are the gate for this work, not an obstacle.
Do not change the EXPR$ prefix or the $<n> form.

If the diff touches build_plan_alias_keys it must also touch the runtime readers in the same commit — select.rs::get_expression_name, accumulator.rs::generate_field_name, or their call sites in processors/select/group_by.rs and processors/group_by_columnar.rs. Producer-alone is the one-sided edit that failed 48 tests.
Do not change a public signature with callers outside plan/ and execution/ — STOP and report instead.

Do not apply the scope tripwire to required work: edits under tests/, the parent mod.rs registrations, docs/sql/PARSER_GRAMMAR.md, and agent.log are mandatory, not scope creep. The tripwire covers src/ only.
Do not change the output name of an item carrying an explicit AS alias — diff-checkable at the naming helper, and the three alias canaries are the runtime check.

Do not touch __exists__, __raw__, or __velostream_variant — legitimate internal sentinels. __agg__ is DIFFERENT and is IN SCOPE: an earlier forbidden entry called it out of scope, which contradicted acceptance bar 2. The Aggregate plan schema names an unaliased top-level aggregate slot UNNAMED_AGGREGATE_PLACEHOLDER (__agg__) while the runtime emits EXPR$<n> for that same slot, so plan and record disagree — and bar 2 requires them equal. Migrate __agg__ to the positional name like any other generated output name.
stop_conditions: The shared helper cannot be reached from execution without changing a public signature whose callers live outside plan/ and execution/.
Preserving the alias_keys write/read contract and shipping EXPR$<n> at execution turn out to be mutually exclusive.

A coupled test requires a changed expectation that is NOT a legacy generated name for an unaliased item — i.e. it pins an explicit AS alias, or a non-naming property (row counts, values, ordering, watermarks). Updating a LEGACY GENERATED name (SUM(...), SUM(expr), __expr__, __group__, price_Multiply_quantity) on an UNALIASED item is EXPECTED WORK, not a stop: log one CHANGED-EXPECTATION line per test and continue to a green sweep. There are ~54 such tests across ~11 modules; stopping on them individually cannot converge, and an earlier version of this condition forbade exactly the work the acceptance bars require, which halted a run that was doing the right thing.

Any of the 8 fail_to_pass tests PASSES against unfixed code (the guard explicit_alias_survives_positional_naming is exempt and must NOT be reported here) — you cannot record a RED-FIRST line for a test that was never red, and must not loosen it until it fails. Either the test does not reach the path it claims, or the bar's premise is wrong; a human decides which.
The __group__ fix cannot be made without changing the output name of a SelectField::AliasedColumn, or of a GROUP BY key carrying an explicit AS alias.
The scope tripwire fires: a file under src/ that neither names an expression nor reads one of the three generators needs editing.

The work produces any ALIAS-KEYS or CHANGED-EXPECTATION conclusion that cannot be recorded in agent.log — the worker does not open the PR, so agent.log plus the final report are the only handoff channels to the caller.

A test pinning an EXPLICIT AS alias fails, or a non-naming property fails (row counts, values, ordering, watermarks). Those are real regressions, not expectation drift, and must not be 'fixed' by editing the expectation.

The CHANGED-EXPECTATION line count does not equal the number of pre-existing tests whose assertion lines the diff modifies. Report both counts and the discrepancy rather than adding lines to make the totals agree.

A test expectation edit changes anything other than a legacy generated-name literal becoming EXPR$<n> — a count, an operator, an added or deleted assertion. Report the hunk; do not reshape the test to fit.
